validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONCERN. The entity 'West Qurna-Baghdad Gas Pipeline' (240 MMcf/d, start 1983, no length, no diameter, FuelSource 'Al-Qurnah', Owner Iraq Ministry of Oil 100%) is traceable ONLY to GEM. (1) The worklist status/fuel/type/start/capacity ref is a JCCP conference PDF that now 404s (verified FAIL). (2) The single gem.wiki outbound citation is 'Iraq Company Laws and Regulations Handbook', International Business Publications (IBP), 2015, p.276 via a Google Books search for 'qurna baghdad pipeline 240' -- IBP handbooks are auto-compiled, low-reliability, and the Google Books page exposes no confirming text (only bibliographic/nav content); it is unverifiable and would be rejected regardless. (3) English + Arabic web searches surface NO independent source naming a West Qurna-to-Baghdad gas line: Arabic Iraqi energy press (Aljazeera, attaqa, al-mosul, infoplus) shows only the West Qurna oil field, the West Qurna-2 associated-gas processing plant (Italian contractor, 2023), and a LOCAL West Qurna gas power station in Basra -- with a possible NEW short feeder to that plant by 2028, not a historic trunk to Baghdad. What IS real: a national gas network 'from the south to Baghdad and the center' built in the 1970s-80s under the South Gas Project (rawabetcenter history; Basrah Gas Company gathers Rumaila, West Qurna 1, Zubair associated gas). That corridor is already represented in GEM by other rows -- so this row is most likely a mislabeled/IBP-derived duplicate of the South Gas -> Baghdad trunk rather than a distinct pipe. DUPLICATE/OVERLAP: strongest overlap is with P4061 'National Gas Pipeline' (600 km, 42 in, ?->Basra, the south-center national trunk) and the Trans-Iraq family (P1852 Trans-Iraq-Nasriyaha 470 km 42 in; P1851 Rumela-Nasriyaha; P2234 North Rumela-Khor Al-Zubair); GEM separately carries a 'West Qurna-Rumela Gas Pipeline' page, reinforcing that these 'West Qurna-X' gas rows are a same-source cluster. ATTRIBUTION: 'West Qurna' as the gas SOURCE is weak -- southern dry gas is dominated by Rumaila, not West Qurna; FuelSource 'Al-Qurnah' has no independent support. SPEC: capacity 240 MMcf/d, start year 1983, length/diameter all lack any independent corroboration (the '240' that appears in modern sources is West Qurna water-injection bpd, not gas MMcf/d). No independent source could be verified that agrees with any GEM number here. Sources below are the independent material I checked; they establish the general south->Baghdad network but do NOT confirm this named entity -- hence low tier / existence concern.

routes.corridor_desc: If this entity is real at all, it would run NNW ~500-550 km straight-line (600+ km by route) from the West Qurna field cluster north of Basra, up the Tigris-Euphrates corridor through Dhi Qar (Nasiriyah) and Wasit (Kut) to Baghdad -- i.e. the SAME south-to-center corridor as GEM's National Gas Pipeline (P4061) and the Trans-Iraq gas family. Endpoints are defensible (West Qurna field and Baghdad are well-located); the intermediate corridor and any station points are INFERRED from the general South Gas national network, not from a route source specific to this line. Bound is loose. Given the open existence/duplicate concern, do not build a route for this PID until the entity itself is resolved (likely a merge into P4061 / the Trans-Iraq trunk).
routes.researcher_notes: Start coord = West Qurna field, ~65 km NW of Basra city (Arabic sources place it there); ~31.0N 47.4E is defensible for the field cluster. End = Baghdad city center 33.31N 44.36E. Waypoint coords are the real locations of Nasiriyah and Kut, offered as candidate corridor nodes only -- NOT sourced as points on this pipeline. No coordinate fabricated: no station/compressor point could be sourced, so none is asserted. Corridor derived from the documented South Gas -> Baghdad national network (rawabetcenter; Basrah Gas Company), which does not name this specific line.

summary: P1853 West Qurna-Baghdad Gas Pipeline: existence CONCERN -- entity named only by GEM + an unverifiable IBP handbook (status ref 404s); no independent source confirms it, likely a mislabeled duplicate of the South Gas->Baghdad trunk (overlaps National Gas Pipeline P4061 / Trans-Iraq family); route corridor only loosely inferable (low).
